wave: fix/tui-panels-builtin-seed — the regression the previous wave's `--apply` introduced
userReport: 修完了以后，TUI侧边栏有MPD了，但只有MPD了，其他的Panel都没了 — after the fixes the sidebar had MPD and ONLY MPD; every other panel was gone.

rootCause.what: The remedy script's merge seeded itself from an EMPTY list when the row's `sidePanel.panels` leaf was absent, because `mergePanelIds(existing, ids, past)` did `(existing ?? "")`.
rootCause.whyThatIsWrong: `sidePanel.panels` REPLACES the host's default rather than extending it, and the host bundle's own patch declares no `panels` leaf — so a profile whose user layer is unset is running on the installed module's `DEFAULT_SIDE_PANEL_IDS` (todo,jobs,agents,info,trajectory,workspace,btw,companion). Seeding from an empty list therefore wrote ONLY our two ids, and the host then applied that as the config, replacing every builtin. The runtime keeper could not repair it either: a CSV that names any of our ids is a POSITION it must not overrule, so it stands down.
measuredTrace: the earlier `--apply` printed: `panels (before): (unset)` / `panels (after): act1:team,act1:workmate` / `added: act1:team,act1:workmate; pruned: (none); kept: (none)` — the empty `kept` list IS the defect
the damaged profile then read: `panels: "act1:team,act1:workmate"` (8 builtins gone) while the host default was `todo,jobs,agents,info,trajectory,workspace,btw,companion`

fix.prevention: `mergePanelIds` takes a fourth parameter `defaultWhenAbsent`, and the write path passes the host's own current default (read from the INSTALLED module, `<profile>/node_modules/@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui/lib/types/tuiDisplayPrefs.js` — the same source the runtime adapter's `probeHostPrefs` reads, never hard-coded).
fix.repair: NEW `resolvePanelSeed(current, hostDefault)` decides the seed in three cases: (a) the leaf is ABSENT -> the host default is the seed; (b) the leaf EXISTS and names NONE of the host's current builtins -> that is the seedless-write DAMAGE, so the default is prepended with the leaf's own tokens preserved after it and the restored ids reported; (c) the leaf names ANY builtin -> a POSITION (however partial) and the seed is the leaf byte-for-byte.
fix.refuseFirst: with no readable host default an ABSENT leaf now REFUSES (exit 1) instead of seeding an empty list; an EXISTING leaf stays usable.
fix.earlyExit: the 'already enabled' early return now also requires `seed.restored.length === 0`, so a restoration can never be swallowed by it (the damaged leaf's ids are already present, so `added` was empty).
fix.declaredResidual: a user who deliberately removes EVERY builtin reads exactly like the damage and is repaired once more — the mirror of the runtime keeper's already-documented residual for the case where every id of OURS is removed.
